data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Jury theorems assume a shared, independent signal of the truth; panelists may have correlated training biases that break independence.","Checklists are artificially constrained to explicit features, unlike jury models that allow gestalt intuition.","Jury models typically assume voters share competence; non-experts may have highly variable base competence."],"overturn_conditions":["If one observes high inter-panel correlation on errors that the expert avoids, the conditional independence assumption is false.","If the expert outperforms the panel on items where the checklist aligns with the expert's explicit reasoning, the reliability gain is an artifact of task simplicity, not a general principle.","If increased panel size does not reduce variance, the ensemble mechanism is absent."],"shared_structure":["Both involve a structured decision rule and a committee of independent voters whose collective judgment aims to capture an objective outcome.","Both use conditional independence of voter errors given the decision rule to drive reliable aggregation.","In both, the completeness of the explicit rule relative to the target's generative structure determines success."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001","SRC_006"],"transfer_claims":["The jury theorem implies that if conditional independence holds and average panelist competence exceeds a threshold, panel reliability approaches perfect accuracy as panel size grows.","Just as juries can fail when voters share a common blind spot (e.g., a biased heuristic), checklist panels will systematically co-fail on items requiring unlisted features.","The completeness of the checklist is analogous to the voters' access to the true signal; an incomplete checklist creates a systematic bias that aggregation cannot remove."]},"claim":"The covering principle is that panel reliability strictly dominates expert intuition whenever (i) the checklist enumerates the complete set of features on which the objectively verifiable outcome depends, and (ii) the non-experts' conditionally independent votes collectively ensemble-average away residual classification noise. Within a single evaluation, the distinguishing evidence is a pattern: high consensus panels systematically err on the same specific items where the expert succeeds\u2014showing that an unlisted cue drives the outcome; if no such systematic co-failure occurs, the gain is genuine.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the checklist omits outcome-relevant features that expert intuition captures, the expert will systematically outperform on items requiring those features, falsifying panel superiority.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If panel members' votes are conditionally dependent (e.g., through shared training biases), ensemble averaging does not reduce residual noise, undermining the reliability mechanism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the task's feature space is too complex for explicit enumeration, the checklist cannot serve as a complete decision rule, and the covering principle collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert's calibration is high and the task distribution is narrow, the stochastic advantage of the ensemble may be negligible.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the objective outcome is sensitive to a continuously interacting threshold that a discrete checklist cannot approximate, the mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Expert intuition tacitly encodes feature-use cues through fast-and-frugal pattern matching but suffers from inconsistent retrieval, anchoring, and attention lapses. The checklist substitutes a deterministic decision rule, while the panel acts as a bagging-style ensemble. Conditional on the checklist, the only residual variance is classification noise; independence ensures aggregation drives this noise toward a reliable expected signal.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
